Postcondition: the session identifier, remember-me series, refresh tokens, and channel-specific sessions are revoked, federated logout is propagated, and the response clears cookies with matching scope. Replaying any pre-logout credential fails, and cached pages are not restored without re-authentication.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-06: Complete Session Termination Invariant

rule_constraints.server: logout deletes the server-side session record
rule_constraints.tokens: all derived tokens and remember-me series revoked
rule_constraints.federation: identity provider logout invoked where applicable
rule_constraints.transport: logout requires POST with CSRF token

text: Security invariant: sessions expire server-side after a short idle period and an absolute maximum lifetime, regardless of client behavior. Precondition: a session exists. Postcondition: inactivity beyond the idle threshold invalidates the session, total age beyond the absolute cap invalidates it, and high-risk actions require fresh authentication. Expiry is enforced on every request, not by a client timer, and the user is informed before an interactive timeout.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-07: Bounded Session Lifetime Invariant

rule_constraints.idle: idle timeout <= 15 minutes for sensitive apps

text: Security invariant: session state is namespaced per module and flow, cleared when a flow completes, and never used as the authority for authorization decisions. Precondition: a flow writes state into the session. Postcondition: transient values are removed on completion, keys cannot collide across modules, and authorization derives roles and tenants from server-side records rather than mutable session flags. Every session value is revalidated at the point of use.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-08: Namespaced Immutable Session State Invariant

rule_constraints.lifecycle: clear transient state on flow completion and login
rule_constraints.authority: authorization reads server-side records, not session flags
rule_constraints.validation: session values revalidated at each use

text: Security invariant: session tokens are protected from script and network exposure, bound to contextual signals where feasible, rotated on risk, and monitored for concurrent use. Precondition: a session is established. Postcondition: tokens are unreadable by script and never sent in cleartext, anomalous context changes trigger re-authentication or revocation, concurrent distant sessions raise an alert, and the user can revoke all sessions. High-value actions require step-up even within a valid session.

metadata.title: WSTG-SESS-09: Context-Bound Session Invariant

rule_constraints.binding: token bound to device fingerprint or client certificate where feasible
rule_constraints.rotation: rotate on risk signals and periodically

text: Security invariant: every endpoint accepts only TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with AEAD cipher suites, a valid certificate, and strong key material, and clients validate the chain and hostname. Precondition: a client connects to a TLS endpoint. Postcondition: weak protocols and ciphers are not negotiated, certificates are verified, HSTS enforces HTTPS, and renegotiation is secure. Configuration is scanned continuously and drift raises an alert.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-01: Modern TLS-Only Invariant

rule_constraints.ciphers: AEAD suites only; no RC4, 3DES, NULL, or export
rule_constraints.certificate: valid chain, strong key, correct hostname, not expired
rule_constraints.validation: clients verify certificates and pin where appropriate

text: Security invariant: all encryption uses an AEAD mode or encrypt-then-MAC with a constant-time integrity check, and decryption failures are indistinguishable to the attacker. Precondition: the application encrypts or decrypts attacker-observable data. Postcondition: tampered ciphertext is rejected before plaintext is processed, padding and content errors return one uniform response, and timing does not depend on validity. Keys are managed centrally, IVs are random and unique, and legacy CBC code is migrated.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-02: Authenticated Encryption Invariant

rule_constraints.mode: AEAD such as AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305

text: Security invariant: every channel that carries credentials, personal data, tokens, or security-relevant telemetry uses authenticated TLS, including internal service-to-service traffic. Precondition: data classified as sensitive is transmitted. Postcondition: only TLS-protected channels are used, cleartext service ports are disabled or firewalled, certificates are validated, and payloads contain no secrets in URLs or logs. Channel inventory is maintained and new integrations are reviewed before deployment.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-03: Encrypted Channel Invariant for Sensitive Data

rule_constraints.channels: TLS for all external and internal sensitive traffic
rule_constraints.services: no cleartext SMTP, LDAP, SQL, or cache ports
rule_constraints.payloads: no secrets in URLs or logs

text: Security invariant: security-relevant cryptography uses vetted modern primitives with managed keys, random unique IVs, and authenticated modes. Precondition: the application hashes, encrypts, signs, or derives keys. Postcondition: passwords use Argon2id, bcrypt, or scrypt with per-user salts; integrity uses SHA-256 or better; encryption uses AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305 with no ECB; keys live in a KMS and rotate. Home-grown schemes are prohibited, and cryptographic choices are reviewed against current guidance.

metadata.title: WSTG-CRYP-04: Modern Cryptography Invariant

rule_constraints.hashing: SHA-256+ for integrity; Argon2id/bcrypt/scrypt for passwords

text: Security invariant: every reflected value is encoded for its exact output context, and client-side code never writes untrusted data into executable DOM sinks. Precondition: request data is rendered into a response. Postcondition: HTML body, attribute, URL, JavaScript, and CSS contexts each receive correct encoding, DOM sinks use textContent or a sanitizer, and CSP limits inline script. Framework auto-escaping is the default, and every explicit bypass is reviewed.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-01: Context-Aware Output Encoding Invariant

rule_constraints.encoding: HTML, attribute, URL, JS, and CSS encoders per sink
rule_constraints.dom: no untrusted data in innerHTML, document.write, or eval

text: Security invariant: persisted user content is sanitized with a maintained allowlist sanitizer and re-encoded for its render context, so no stored value can execute script. Precondition: user content is stored and later rendered. Postcondition: dangerous tags, attributes, and URL schemes are removed, rich text is sanitized on store and again on render, and every view uses context-aware encoding. CSP blocks inline script, and admin and support views receive the same treatment as public pages.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-02: Stored Content Sanitization Invariant

rule_constraints.sanitize: allowlist HTML sanitizer on input and output
rule_constraints.context: encode per sink at render time
rule_constraints.rich_text: sanitize on store and re-sanitize on render

text: Security invariant: authorization is enforced in the router for every HTTP method a route accepts, and each route explicitly declares its permitted methods. Precondition: a request targets any route. Postcondition: unauthorized requests fail regardless of verb, unlisted methods return 405, method override headers are disabled or restricted to trusted clients, and the same policy applies to HEAD and OPTIONS. Route tests exercise every method in CI.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-03: Method-Agnostic Authorization Invariant

rule_constraints.authorization: evaluated in the router for every method
rule_constraints.override: method override headers disabled or validated

text: Security invariant: every tier parses parameters identically, and duplicate or ambiguous names are rejected or canonicalized before any security decision. Precondition: a request carries parameters. Postcondition: only one value per name reaches the application, arrays are explicitly typed, encoded variants are normalized, and the WAF and origin share a parser or a normalized representation. Schemas reject unexpected multiplicity, and tests cover duplicate-name cases.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-04: Canonical Single-Value Parameter Invariant

rule_constraints.consistency: edge and origin use the same parser
rule_constraints.security: decisions use the canonical parsed value

text: Security invariant: all SQL values are bound through prepared statements, identifiers come from a fixed allowlist, and the database account holds only the privileges the feature needs. Precondition: a query includes user-influenced data. Postcondition: input never becomes syntax, dynamic identifiers resolve through a map, errors are generic, and ORM raw fragments are reviewed. Escaping is defense in depth only.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-05: Parameterized Query Invariant

text: Security invariant: every user value inserted into an LDAP filter is escaped per RFC 4515, or the directory API is used with parameter binding, and the service account has only the rights required. Precondition: a directory query includes user input. Postcondition: metacharacters cannot change filter logic, wildcard searches are explicit and authorized, errors are generic, and results are limited to the intended scope.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-06: Escaped LDAP Filter Invariant

rule_constraints.scope: bind with a least-privilege service account
rule_constraints.validation: reject control characters and overlong input

text: Security invariant: XML is constructed with a library that escapes text nodes and attributes, validated against a strict schema, and parsed with DTDs and external entities disabled. Precondition: user data enters an XML document. Postcondition: metacharacters cannot create elements, attributes, or comments, duplicate fields are rejected, and signatures cover canonicalized content. String concatenation is prohibited, and parsers enforce the schema before processing.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-07: Safe XML Construction Invariant

rule_constraints.construct: use an XML builder or DOM API, not string concatenation

text: Security invariant: server-side includes are disabled everywhere untrusted content can be written or reflected, and directive syntax is escaped in any user-visible output. Precondition: user content is stored or rendered by the web server. Postcondition: no path containing user content has SSI processing enabled, upload directories do not map to SSI handlers, and server configuration is audited for Includes options.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-08: SSI Disabled for Untrusted Content Invariant

rule_constraints.ssi: disabled on upload and user-content paths
rule_constraints.handler: no SSI mapping for user extensions
rule_constraints.encoding: escape directive syntax in reflected content
rule_constraints.review: server config audited for Options Includes

text: Security invariant: XPath queries use variables or an API that binds values, never string concatenation, and errors do not reveal the expression. Precondition: user input is used in an XPath query. Postcondition: quotes, brackets, and boolean operators cannot change the predicate, the queried node set is limited to the intended scope, and failures are indistinguishable.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-09: Parameterized XPath Invariant

rule_constraints.escape: escape quotes and brackets if concatenation is unavoidable
rule_constraints.scope: limit the queried document and node set

text: Security invariant: mail commands are built through a protocol library with structured fields, and addresses and headers reject CR, LF, and NUL characters. Precondition: user input influences an SMTP or IMAP command. Postcondition: input cannot terminate a command or add a header, recipients are strictly parsed, outbound volume per account is limited, and the server refuses relay to unauthorized domains.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-10: Protocol-Safe Mail Command Invariant

rule_constraints.crlf: reject CR, LF, and NUL in addresses and headers
rule_constraints.api: use a mail library with structured fields

text: Security invariant: untrusted input is never evaluated as code and never controls an include path; resource selection uses a fixed server-side map. Precondition: a feature evaluates expressions or loads files dynamically. Postcondition: eval and equivalent constructs are absent from request paths, include targets come from an allowlist of identifiers, remote and filter wrappers are disabled, and uploaded files cannot be executed. Errors are generic and execution runs under least privilege.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-11: No-Dynamic-Evaluation Invariant

rule_constraints.eval: no eval, assert, or dynamic code from input
rule_constraints.include: paths from a fixed map, never from request data
rule_constraints.upload: uploaded files never reachable by the interpreter

text: Security invariant: external commands are invoked through an argument-array API with shell interpretation disabled, and every user-influenced argument is allowlisted or strongly typed. Precondition: the application invokes an external program. Postcondition: metacharacters have no special meaning, leading dashes cannot inject options, library equivalents replace shell commands where possible, and execution runs under a dedicated low-privilege account with bounded output.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-12: Structured Command Execution Invariant

rule_constraints.validation: strict allowlist or strong typing per argument

text: Security invariant: format strings are constant literals and user data is always passed as an argument, never as the format itself. Precondition: a printf-family or logging API processes user data. Postcondition: conversion specifiers in input are inert, logging uses parameterized calls, and compiler format warnings are enabled and treated as errors. Localization and template formats validate specifiers before use.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-13: Fixed Format String Invariant

rule_constraints.format: constant format literal, input always an argument
rule_constraints.validation: reject or escape % in user-visible format contexts

text: Security invariant: stored data is revalidated and context-encoded at every point of use, regardless of the validation performed at entry. Precondition: data crosses a component, job, or time boundary. Postcondition: each consumer applies its own schema, type, and encoding controls, background jobs treat stored data as untrusted, and provenance and classification travel with the data. Entry validation is defense in depth, never a substitute for sink protection.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-14: Revalidate-at-Use Invariant

rule_constraints.trust: no stored data is trusted by default
rule_constraints.validate: schema and type checks at each consumer
rule_constraints.provenance: data classified at entry and on read

text: Security invariant: every hop in the chain uses a strict, consistent HTTP parser that rejects ambiguous framing and never reflects CRLF into headers. Precondition: a request or response traverses a proxy, load balancer, or origin. Postcondition: messages with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, duplicate framing headers, obs-fold, or CRLF in values are rejected, and all hops share the same normalization rules. Back-end connections are not reused across trust boundaries when framing is uncertain.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-15: Strict HTTP Framing Invariant

rule_constraints.framing: reject ambiguous Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding combinations
rule_constraints.crlf: reject CR and LF in header values
rule_constraints.headers: reject duplicate or obfuscated framing headers
rule_constraints.hops: consistent parser configuration across the chain

text: Security invariant: the server accepts only the request forms and methods its role requires, rejects absolute-form targets and CONNECT unless it is a deliberate proxy, and cannot originate traffic to internal ranges. Precondition: an HTTP request arrives at the web tier. Postcondition: unexpected forms and methods return 400 or 405, proxy headers are ignored, and egress policy prevents the web tier from reaching internal services. Request parsing is reviewed whenever a proxy or gateway is introduced.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-16: Explicit Request Surface Invariant

rule_constraints.egress: block server-originated traffic to internal ranges

text: Security invariant: absolute URLs and virtual-host routing derive from a configured canonical origin, and the Host header is validated against an allowlist before any use. Precondition: a request supplies Host or forwarding headers. Postcondition: unknown hosts are rejected or served a default, reset and notification links use the configured origin, and X-Forwarded-Host is honored only from a trusted proxy. Cache keys include the canonical host.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-17: Configured Canonical Host Invariant

rule_constraints.url: build absolute URLs from configured canonical origin
rule_constraints.forward: ignore X-Forwarded-Host unless from a trusted proxy

text: Security invariant: templates are authored by developers and user input is passed only as data variables, never concatenated into template source. Precondition: a feature renders a template with user-influenced values. Postcondition: expressions in input are inert, preview and email builders use predefined templates, and any dynamic template feature is sandboxed with a restricted context. The template engine is reviewed for reachable gadget objects.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-18: Template Data Separation Invariant

rule_constraints.render: templates are static; user data passed as variables

text: Security invariant: server-side fetches are restricted to an explicit allowlist and validated against the resolved IP after DNS resolution, with every redirect hop revalidated. Precondition: the server fetches a URL influenced by an external actor. Postcondition: private, loopback, link-local, and metadata ranges are unreachable, DNS rebinding is defeated by address pinning, egress policy enforces the same boundary, and responses are bounded and never returned raw.

metadata.title: WSTG-INPV-19: Resolved-Destination Invariant

rule_constraints.resolve: validate the resolved IP, not the string

text: Security invariant: a session is created only from a token that the server validates directly with the identity provider, and the session subject is the verified subject claim rather than any value supplied by the browser. Precondition: a user completes an OAuth login. Postcondition: the authorization code is exchanged back-channel, the signature, issuer, audience, expiry, and nonce are verified, the code is single-use, and the email or username in the request body is ignored. Implicit flow is disabled in favour of authorization code with PKCE.

metadata.title: OAuth Implicit Flow Authentication Bypass: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.flow: authorization code with PKCE; implicit flow disabled
rule_constraints.validation: verify signature, iss, aud, exp, and nonce server-side
rule_constraints.binding: session subject comes from the verified token, never a request body
rule_constraints.replay: single-use code, short-lived tokens, nonce checked

text: Security invariant: every OAuth linking and unlinking operation requires an unguessable state value bound to the authenticated session, and the operation is confirmed with fresh authentication. Precondition: a user initiates or completes an identity link. Postcondition: a request that does not carry the matching single-use state is rejected, the flow cannot be completed by a different session, the account owner receives a notification, and unlinking is equally protected. Linking a social identity is treated as a credential change, not a preference update.

metadata.title: Forced OAuth Profile Linking: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.state: cryptographic state bound to the session, single-use
rule_constraints.notify: email notification on identity link and unlink
rule_constraints.scope: linking and unlinking require the current password or MFA

text: Security invariant: redirect_uri must exactly match a pre-registered value and the authorization code is bound to that value, the client, and a PKCE verifier. Precondition: a client starts an authorization request. Postcondition: any redirect_uri with extra segments, encoded traversal, or a different host is rejected before the code is issued, the code is single-use and short-lived, and exchange fails unless the verifier and exact redirect match. Open redirects on the client are treated as an OAuth-critical defect.

metadata.title: OAuth Account Hijacking via redirect_uri: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.redirect: exact string match against registered URIs; no wildcards or traversal
rule_constraints.binding: authorization code bound to client and exact redirect_uri

text: Security invariant: access tokens never travel in a URL that can be redirected, and the client exposes no open redirect that could receive one. Precondition: an OAuth flow completes. Postcondition: the authorization code flow with PKCE replaces implicit flow, tokens are returned only to the exact registered callback over a back channel or fragment that cannot be forwarded, redirect destinations are allowlisted, and tokens have a narrow audience and short lifetime. Any open redirect is treated as an OAuth compromise primitive.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.redirect: no open redirect on the client; destination allowlist
rule_constraints.tokens: authorization code flow; tokens never in URLs
rule_constraints.fragment: token delivered only to the exact registered callback
rule_constraints.binding: token audience restricted to the client API

associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via Open Redirect

text: Security invariant: cross-origin messages carrying credentials are sent only to an explicit trusted origin, and every listener validates event.origin before acting. Precondition: a page uses postMessage or can be framed. Postcondition: the target origin is never a wildcard for sensitive data, listeners reject messages from unknown origins, authentication pages set frame-ancestors to none, and tokens never appear in the URL of a page that can be embedded. Token-bearing pages are excluded from third-party framing entirely.

metadata.title: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.origin: postMessage targetOrigin is an explicit trusted origin
rule_constraints.framing: frame-ancestors restricts embedding of auth pages
rule_constraints.token: tokens never placed in a framable page URL

associated_labs: OAuth Access Token Theft via a Proxy Page

text: Security invariant: no claim from a JWT is read until the signature has been verified with a pinned algorithm and a trusted key, and the issuer, audience, expiry, and not-before claims are validated. Precondition: a request presents a JWT. Postcondition: a token with an invalid, missing, or unexpected signature is rejected before any authorization decision, verification uses strict library mode rather than decode-only helpers, and failures return a generic 401. Tests assert that a tampered payload is rejected.

metadata.title: JWT Unverified Signature Bypass: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.verify: every JWT is signature-verified before any claim is read
rule_constraints.library: strict verification mode with algorithms pinned
rule_constraints.claims: iss, aud, exp, and nbf validated
rule_constraints.fail: verification failure returns 401 without partial processing

text: Security invariant: the verification algorithm is chosen by the server and pinned per key, and the alg header in the token can never select or disable verification. Precondition: a JWT is presented. Postcondition: none and any unexpected algorithm are rejected unconditionally, an empty signature fails, and the library is called with an explicit expected algorithm. Case variants and whitespace in the header do not alter the decision, and tests cover alg=none submissions.

metadata.title: JWT alg=none Acceptance: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.algorithm: server pins the expected algorithm; header alg ignored
rule_constraints.signature: empty signature segment is a hard failure
rule_constraints.library: verification API that requires an explicit algorithm

text: Security invariant: JWT signing keys have at least 256 bits of entropy, live in a managed secret store, rotate on a schedule, and are never shared between environments or embedded in source. Precondition: a service signs or verifies tokens. Postcondition: HMAC secrets are generated with a CSPRNG, asymmetric keys are preferred for multi-service identity, key identifiers allow rotation without invalidating all sessions, and exposure triggers immediate revocation. Key strength is checked during provisioning.

metadata.title: JWT Weak Signing Key: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.entropy: HMAC secret >= 256 bits from a CSPRNG
rule_constraints.storage: secret in a KMS or secret manager, never in source

text: Security invariant: verification keys come only from a server-side trusted key store selected by a validated key identifier, and key material embedded in the token is never trusted. Precondition: a JWT with a key header is presented. Postcondition: jwk and jku headers are ignored or rejected, kid is matched against a fixed map, the algorithm is pinned per key, and a token that supplies its own key fails verification. Key rotation uses published JWKS from a trusted origin.

metadata.title: JWT jwk Header Injection: Defensive Invariants

rule_constraints.key: verification keys resolved only from a server-side trusted store
rule_constraints.jwk: jwk and jku headers ignored or rejected
rule_constraints.kid: kid maps to a known key, never to key material

text: Security invariant: remote key sets are fetched only from a fixed allowlist of trusted HTTPS origins, never from a URL chosen by the token, and retrieval fails closed. Precondition: a JWT references a remote key set. Postcondition: jku values outside the allowlist are rejected before any request, redirects are not followed, TLS is verified, responses are size-bounded, and keys are cached per issuer so a hostile set cannot contaminate other tenants. rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker holds a session without the second factor
rule_constraints.postcondition: suppress sensitive diagnostics and require fresh factor for sensitive changes

text: Security invariant: the server creates the authenticated session only after verifying the code, and every protected request checks that verification completed. Precondition: the attacker holds valid primary credentials. Postcondition: a failed verification leaves no usable session, response flags are not authoritative, and protected endpoints reject sessions that have not completed 2FA.

metadata.title: 2FA Invariant: Server-Side Session Established Only After Code Verification
metadata.report_title: 2FA Bypass via Response Manipulation on Login Page

rule_constraints.invariant: session.authenticated implies session.otp_verified
rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker holds valid primary credentials
rule_constraints.postcondition: issue no authenticated session before OTP verification and re-check on protected requests

text: Security invariant: a checkout confirmation is readable only by the session that placed the order, and the identifier is unguessable and single-use. Precondition: the confirmation page is addressable by a checkout identifier. Postcondition: the server checks order ownership and session binding, expires the key quickly, and applies rate limits to failed lookups.

metadata.title: Checkout Invariant: Confirmation Pages Are Bound to the Buyer Session
metadata.report_title: Bypassing one-time checkout router page (revealing payment information)

rule_constraints.invariant: order.session == request.session and checkout_key.high_entropy and not expired
rule_constraints.precondition: the confirmation page accepts a checkout identifier
rule_constraints.postcondition: verify ownership and expire the key after first display

text: Security invariant: trusted-device state is bound to the verified identity and is revoked on any change to the account identifier or primary factor. Precondition: the product offers a trust-this-device option. Postcondition: an email or phone change clears trust, requires the new identifier to be verified, and forces 2FA on the next authentication.

metadata.title: Trusted-Device Invariant: Scope Is Bound to the Verified Identity
metadata.report_title: 2FA Bypass leads to impersonation of legitimate users

rule_constraints.invariant: device_trust.identity == account.verified_identity and trust revoked on identifier change
rule_constraints.precondition: the product supports trusted devices
rule_constraints.postcondition: revoke trust and require verification after an identifier change

text: Security invariant: publication transitions are performed only by an authorized reviewer, and the content owner cannot set the approved state. Precondition: vacancies require moderation before publication. Postcondition: owner mutations are limited to draft and pending, reviewer transitions are recorded with an actor, and public visibility requires a recorded approval for the current content version.

metadata.title: Moderation Invariant: Publication Requires an Approved Review State
metadata.report_title: inDriver Job - Admin Approval Bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: vacancy.status == published implies approval.recorded(vacancy, content_version)
rule_constraints.precondition: vacancies require moderation before publication
rule_constraints.postcondition: restrict owner transitions and require a recorded approval for the current content

text: Security invariant: loyalty value accrues only from settled, non-refundable revenue and is reversed when the underlying order is cancelled, refunded, or returned. Precondition: the store credits points from order status. Postcondition: accrual waits for a settlement event, points remain pending until then, and every reversal is atomic with the refund.

metadata.title: Points Invariant: Rewards Accrue Only on Settled Revenue
metadata.report_title: Gaining unlimited bonus points on websites with WooCommerce Points and Rewards

rule_constraints.invariant: points.credited implies order.settled and points reversed on cancellation
rule_constraints.precondition: the store credits points based on order status
rule_constraints.postcondition: accrue on settlement and reverse on cancellation or refund

text: Security invariant: billing pages and payment actions require the billing-administrator role on the server, regardless of navigation state. Precondition: the organization has members without billing rights. Postcondition: the route and every billing API reject non-billing roles, and the denial is uniform so it does not disclose billing configuration.

metadata.title: Billing Invariant: Payment Methods Restricted to Billing Administrators
metadata.report_title: A member-member privilege could access the billing payment page even though the billing page is hidden from the menu

rule_constraints.invariant: role.includes(billing_admin) before billing.read_or_write
rule_constraints.precondition: members exist without billing rights
rule_constraints.postcondition: deny billing routes and actions for non-billing roles

text: Security invariant: subscription requests are limited per target address, per source, and per time window, and a new subscription requires confirmation from the mailbox. Precondition: the endpoint is public. Postcondition: repeated requests for the same address are coalesced, volume limits apply regardless of pacing, and unconfirmed addresses are not subscribed.

metadata.title: Subscription Invariant: Per-Address and Per-Client Throttling
metadata.report_title: No rate limit in email subscription

rule_constraints.invariant: requests_per_address <= limit and requests_per_source <= limit and confirmation_required
rule_constraints.precondition: the subscription endpoint is publicly reachable
rule_constraints.postcondition: coalesce repeats and require mailbox confirmation

text: Security invariant: an email confirmation code allows a small bounded number of attempts, expires quickly, and is invalidated by a new request; enrolment requires a verified email and a verified new factor. Precondition: 2FA setup requires email confirmation. Postcondition: excess attempts lock the challenge, the old code dies on reissue, and factor binding requires both proofs.

metadata.title: Enrolment Invariant: Bounded Email-Code Attempts
metadata.report_title: Email Verification Bypass by bruteforcing when setting up 2FA

rule_constraints.invariant: email_code.attempts <= max and code invalidated on reissue
rule_constraints.precondition: 2FA setup requires email confirmation
rule_constraints.postcondition: lock on excess attempts and require verified email before binding

text: Security invariant: a factor can be linked only to the account of the authenticated principal, and verification requires primary authentication in the same flow. Precondition: the linking and verification endpoints accept an account identifier. Postcondition: the identifier is derived from the session, the link requires password or existing-factor proof, and login by factor alone is impossible.

metadata.title: Factor-Linking Invariant: Session-Bound Identity and Verified Possession
metadata.report_title: Account takeover w/o interaction for a user that doesn't have 2fa enabled via 2fa linking and improper auth at /api/2fa/verify

rule_constraints.invariant: link.user_id == session.principal and primary_auth_verified before factor.bound
rule_constraints.precondition: the linking endpoint accepts a user identifier
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive identity from the session and require primary authentication

text: Security invariant: each MFA challenge permits a small number of attempts, rotates or locks after the budget, and raises an alert on abnormal volume. Precondition: the attacker holds the primary credential. Postcondition: excess attempts invalidate the challenge, the code cannot be swept, and the account owner is notified.

metadata.title: MFA Invariant: Attempt Budget and Code Rotation
metadata.report_title: 2FA bypass possible on https://authsvc.singlestore.com

rule_constraints.invariant: mfa.attempts <= max_attempts and challenge locked on exhaustion
rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker holds the primary credential
rule_constraints.postcondition: lock the challenge after the attempt budget and alert on volume

text: Security invariant: a value-bearing promotion action requires strong, fresh authentication, rate limiting per token and per source, and a uniform response that does not confirm token validity. Precondition: the endpoint accepts a bearer token. Postcondition: guessing is bounded, failures are blacklisted, and promotion eligibility is checked against the authenticated account.

metadata.title: Promotion Invariant: Promotion Actions Require Strong Authentication and Rate Limits
metadata.report_title: The Uber Promo Customer Endpoint Does Not Implement Multifactor Authentication, Blacklisting or Rate Limiting

rule_constraints.invariant: requests_per_token <= limit and strong_auth and uniform_response
rule_constraints.precondition: the promotion endpoint accepts a bearer token
rule_constraints.postcondition: throttle per token and source and require strong authentication

text: Security invariant: every submission channel evaluates the same program eligibility rules against the same actor and target before creating a report. Precondition: a program configures a requirement or blacklist. Postcondition: the shared gate rejects ineligible submissions on web, embedded, API, and mobile channels, and the rejection is recorded.

metadata.title: Submission Invariant: Every Channel Applies the Same Eligibility Rules
metadata.report_title: Hacker can bypass 2FA requirement and reporter blacklist through embedded submission form

rule_constraints.invariant: policy.eligible(actor, program) before report.created on every channel
rule_constraints.precondition: programs can configure submission requirements
rule_constraints.postcondition: enforce the same eligibility gate across all channels

text: Security invariant: the identity provisioned is the identity verified in the same signup session, and the provisioning endpoint accepts only a server-side reference to that session. Precondition: signup provisions an account from request data. Postcondition: the identifier cannot be substituted, verification and provisioning read the same stored value, and the session is consumed once.

metadata.title: Signup Invariant: Provisioned Identity Must Match the Verified Applicant
metadata.report_title: Email verification bypass via request to endpoint accounts.insightly.com/signup/provisionuser

rule_constraints.invariant: provision.email == session.verified_email
rule_constraints.precondition: signup accepts an email parameter and provisions an account
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive the identity from the session and reject substitution

text: Security invariant: folder creation checks and consumes quota in one atomic operation, and the stored count can never exceed the plan limit. Precondition: the space has a finite folder quota. Postcondition: concurrent creates serialize on a quota row or constraint, losers are rejected, and the count is authoritative.

metadata.title: Folder Invariant: Quota Enforced Atomically at Creation
metadata.report_title: Race Condition in Folder Creation Allows Bypassing Folder Limit

rule_constraints.invariant: folder_count <= plan_limit at commit time
rule_constraints.precondition: the space has a finite folder quota
rule_constraints.postcondition: serialize count-and-create and reject requests that exceed the limit

text: Security invariant: an invitation is valid only while its inviter retains the authority to grant the invited role, and removing the inviter revokes or re-reviews every grant it created. Precondition: a team admin can invite peers with equal privileges. Postcondition: inviter removal cascades to pending invitations and triggers review of memberships created by that inviter.

metadata.title: Invitation Invariant: Grants Inherit the Inviter's Current Authority
metadata.report_title: Pending invites remain valid even after the inviter is removed.

rule_constraints.invariant: invite.valid implies inviter.has_role(invite.role)
rule_constraints.precondition: admins can invite peers with admin privileges
rule_constraints.postcondition: revoke pending invites on inviter removal and review accepted memberships

text: Security invariant: every quantity is a positive integer, the total is computed server-side from catalogue prices, and the charged amount is reconciled against the line items before authorization. Precondition: the bulk endpoint accepts per-item quantities. Postcondition: negative and zero quantities are rejected, totals are recomputed from the server catalogue, and any mismatch blocks the order.

metadata.title: Cart Invariant: Quantity and Line Totals Are Non-Negative and Server-Computed
metadata.report_title: An attacker can buy marketplace articles for lower prices as it allows for negative quantity values

rule_constraints.invariant: quantity > 0 and total == sum(catalogue_price * quantity)
rule_constraints.precondition: the endpoint accepts per-item quantities
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject non-positive quantities and recompute the total server-side

text: Security invariant: program eligibility rules are structured, evaluated before an invitation is issued, and re-evaluated when the invitation is accepted. Precondition: a program declares participation restrictions. Postcondition: ineligible researchers receive no invitation, acceptance re-checks the rules, and the evaluation is recorded for compliance.

metadata.title: Eligibility Invariant: Program Rules Evaluated Before Invitation
metadata.report_title: Proper verification is not done before sending invitations to researchers for certain private programs with rules e.g. Participants must be US-based

rule_constraints.invariant: eligible(researcher, program.rules) before invite.issued and before participation
rule_constraints.precondition: a program declares participation restrictions
rule_constraints.postcondition: evaluate structured rules before issuance and at acceptance

text: Security invariant: email addresses and domains are canonicalized with Unicode normalization, case folding, and IDNA before any policy comparison or delivery decision. Precondition: the tenant can deny specific domains. Postcondition: alternate representations match the denylist, delivery uses the canonical domain, and ambiguous addresses are rejected.

metadata.title: Domain Restriction Invariant: Canonical Domain Match Before Invitation
metadata.report_title: Bypassing the block of Security Domain Restriction and normally invite blocked domains with special characters

rule_constraints.invariant: canonical(domain(address)) not in denied_domains before invitation.sent
rule_constraints.precondition: the tenant configures denied domains
rule_constraints.postcondition: canonicalize before matching and before delivery

text: Security invariant: a transcript is retrievable only by a principal who participated in the conversation, and the object is addressed by an unguessable reference resolved server-side. Precondition: transcripts are stored and served as files. Postcondition: the server maps the reference to an owner and rejects foreign access, and static paths are not enumerable.

metadata.title: Transcript Invariant: File Access Requires Ownership of the Conversation
metadata.lab_title: Insecure direct object references

rule_constraints.invariant: transcript.owner in request.principal.participants
rule_constraints.precondition: transcripts are addressable by a client-supplied filename
rule_constraints.postcondition: resolve the object server-side and verify participation before returning content

text: Security invariant: a privileged operation checks the actor's role on the server regardless of the HTTP method, and unprivileged callers cannot reach the same handler. Precondition: the promotion endpoint is used by administrators. Postcondition: every method is authorized against the role, method-override headers are ignored, and the promotion is recorded with the actor.

metadata.title: Role Invariant: Promotion Requires an Authorized Actor, Not a Method
metadata.lab_title: Method-based access control can be circumvented

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, admin) before role.change
rule_constraints.precondition: the promotion endpoint is reachable with multiple methods
rule_constraints.postcondition: authorize the actor role on every method and record the change

text: Security invariant: every step of a privileged workflow independently authorizes the actor and validates the workflow state server-side. Precondition: role changes use a multi-step process. Postcondition: the server records the initiated request, refuses confirmation without it, and checks the actor's role at each transition.

metadata.title: Workflow Invariant: Every Step Enforces the Same Authorization
metadata.lab_title: Multi-step process with no access control on one step

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, admin) and workflow.state == initiated at every step
rule_constraints.precondition: the promotion workflow has multiple steps
rule_constraints.postcondition: authorize each step and bind confirmation to a server-side workflow state

text: Security invariant: authorization is based on the authenticated actor's role, and client-controlled headers such as Referer and Origin are never treated as entitlement. Precondition: the endpoint inspects Referer. Postcondition: the role check runs regardless of headers, and the promotion is attributed to the actor.

metadata.title: Origin Invariant: Referer Is Not an Authorization Credential
metadata.lab_title: Referer-based access control

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, admin) before role.change
rule_constraints.precondition: the endpoint inspects the Referer header
rule_constraints.postcondition: ignore Referer for authorization and check the actor's role

text: Security invariant: every administrative route and action requires an authenticated actor with the administrative role, and discovery artifacts do not disclose restricted paths. Precondition: an admin panel exists. Postcondition: anonymous and non-admin requests are denied, and robots.txt lists no restricted routes.

metadata.title: Admin Invariant: Administrative Functions Require an Authorized Role
metadata.lab_title: Unprotected admin functionality

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, admin) before admin.route_or_action
rule_constraints.precondition: an administrative panel exists
rule_constraints.postcondition: deny anonymous access and remove restricted paths from discovery files

text: Security invariant: an administrative route is protected by a server-side role check, and its path is not treated as a secret. Precondition: the panel has an unpredictable path. Postcondition: direct requests are denied without the role, and client assets do not disclose restricted routes.

metadata.title: Admin Invariant: Obscurity Is Not Authorization
metadata.lab_title: Unprotected admin functionality with unpredictable URL

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, admin) before admin.route_or_action
rule_constraints.precondition: the admin panel uses an obscure path
rule_constraints.postcondition: enforce the role check and remove the path from client assets

text: Security invariant: the path authorized at the edge is the path executed by the backend, and administrative routes require a server-side role check. Precondition: the edge blocks paths while the backend honors routing headers. Postcondition: routing headers from untrusted clients are stripped, and the panel authorizes every request.

metadata.title: Routing Invariant: Front-End and Backend Agree on the Authorized Path
metadata.lab_title: URL-based access control can be circumvented

rule_constraints.invariant: edge.path == backend.path and has_role(actor, admin)
rule_constraints.precondition: the edge blocks paths and the backend honors routing headers
rule_constraints.postcondition: strip routing headers and authorize the admin role

text: Security invariant: profile data is selected by the authenticated principal, and any identifier in the request is verified against that principal before use. Precondition: the account page accepts a user identifier. Postcondition: the server ignores client-supplied identity or rejects mismatch, and credentials are not rendered in profile responses.

metadata.title: Account Invariant: Profile Data Scoped to the Session Principal
metadata.lab_title: User ID controlled by request parameter

rule_constraints.invariant: profile.user == session.principal
rule_constraints.precondition: the account page accepts a user identifier
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive the profile from the session and reject mismatched identifiers

text: Security invariant: an unauthorized request produces no foreign data in any part of the response, including redirect bodies, and the object is not loaded before authorization. Precondition: the page redirects on mismatch. Postcondition: authorize before loading, and emit an empty denial body.

metadata.title: Redirect Invariant: Denials Carry No Foreign Data in the Body
metadata.lab_title: User ID controlled by request parameter with data leakage in redirect

rule_constraints.invariant: authorized before load and denial_body contains no foreign_data
rule_constraints.precondition: the page redirects when the identifier mismatches
rule_constraints.postcondition: check ownership first and emit no data on denial

text: Security invariant: passwords are stored irreversibly and are never rendered to any client, and profile data is scoped to the session principal. Precondition: the account page accepts a user identifier. Postcondition: no password field is populated, the profile is derived from the session, and credentials are not decryptable for display.

metadata.title: Profile Invariant: Stored Passwords Never Rendered to the Client
metadata.lab_title: User ID controlled by request parameter with password disclosure

rule_constraints.invariant: password.never_rendered and profile.user == session.principal
rule_constraints.precondition: the account page accepts a user identifier
rule_constraints.postcondition: remove password rendering and derive the profile from the session

text: Security invariant: a profile is returned only for the session principal, regardless of whether identifiers are sequential, random, or disclosed elsewhere. Precondition: the profile is addressed by a user identifier. Postcondition: ownership is checked server-side, and identifiers are not treated as secrets.

metadata.title: Identifier Invariant: Unguessable IDs Still Require Ownership Checks
metadata.lab_title: User ID controlled by request parameter, with unpredictable user IDs

rule_constraints.invariant: profile.user == session.principal
rule_constraints.precondition: the profile is addressed by a user GUID
rule_constraints.postcondition: ignore the supplied identifier or verify it against the session

text: Security invariant: profile updates bind only allowlisted fields, and role changes require an administrative action with its own authorization and audit. Precondition: the profile update accepts a JSON or form body. Postcondition: unknown and privileged fields are rejected, role is read-only in this context, and the effective role is recomputed server-side.

metadata.title: Profile Invariant: Role Is Not Writable Through the Profile Update
metadata.lab_title: User role can be modified in user profile

rule_constraints.invariant: update.fields subset profile_allowlist and role changed only by admin.action
rule_constraints.precondition: the profile update accepts user-supplied fields
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject role fields and require an administrative role change

text: Security invariant: authorization is resolved from server-side role state on every request, and no cookie can grant or change a role. Precondition: the application stores role information in a cookie. Postcondition: cookies carry only an opaque session reference, the role is loaded server-side, and tampering has no effect.

metadata.title: Role Invariant: Authorization Resolved from Server-Side State
metadata.lab_title: User role controlled by request parameter

rule_constraints.invariant: role == server_state(session).role and cookie does not contain role
rule_constraints.precondition: a role-bearing cookie is issued to the client
rule_constraints.postcondition: resolve the role server-side and ignore client role values

text: Security invariant: every documented operation enforces the same role and object checks as the interface, and documentation is not reachable by unprivileged users in production. Precondition: the API publishes machine-readable or interactive documentation. Postcondition: destructive operations require an administrative role, username parameters are authorized against that role, and the documentation surface is authenticated and access-controlled.

metadata.title: Documentation Invariant: Published Interfaces Still Enforce Role and Object Checks
metadata.lab_title: Exploiting an API endpoint using documentation

rule_constraints.invariant: has_role(actor, user_admin) before user.delete and docs reachable only by authorized roles
rule_constraints.precondition: the API publishes documentation reachable by an ordinary account
rule_constraints.postcondition: authorize destructive operations and gate the documentation surface

text: Security invariant: the order total is derived server-side from the catalogue and the account's real entitlements, and the client can set only line items and quantities. Precondition: checkout accepts an order payload. Postcondition: unknown fields are rejected, discounts are computed from validated promotions, and the charged total is reconciled before the order is created.

metadata.title: Order Invariant: Discounts Are Derived from Server-Side Entitlement
metadata.lab_title: Exploiting a mass assignment vulnerability

rule_constraints.invariant: order.total == server_total(items, entitlements(account))
rule_constraints.precondition: checkout accepts a structured order payload
rule_constraints.postcondition: bind an allowlist and compute discounts from server-side entitlement

text: Security invariant: a route exposes only the methods its purpose requires, and price data is writable only by an administrative pricing role with an audit trail. Precondition: the price route is public and read-only by design. Postcondition: write methods are removed or authorized, the basket reads server-side catalogue prices, and any price change is attributed.

metadata.title: Price Invariant: Client Input Never Sets an Item Price
metadata.lab_title: Exploiting an unused API endpoint

rule_constraints.invariant: route.allowed_methods == ['GET'] for public price routes
rule_constraints.precondition: the price route is reachable by any authenticated shopper
rule_constraints.postcondition: restrict methods and require an administrative role for price changes

text: Security invariant: user input is encoded as a single opaque value before it is placed in any server-side URL, and the internal API validates the complete parameter set it receives. Precondition: the front end composes a backend URL from user input. Postcondition: delimiters in input are encoded, unexpected internal parameters are rejected, and error messages do not enumerate them.

metadata.title: Parameter Invariant: User Input Is Encoded Before Server-Side URL Composition
metadata.lab_title: Exploiting server-side parameter pollution in a query string

rule_constraints.invariant: encode(user_input) and internal.params == expected_param_set
rule_constraints.precondition: the front end composes an internal query from a user-supplied value
rule_constraints.postcondition: encode the value and reject unexpected internal parameters

text: Security invariant: user input is encoded before insertion into a URL path and cannot introduce new segments, and the internal API authorizes the caller for the specific resource. Precondition: the front end builds a REST path from user input. Postcondition: traversal and encoded separators are rejected, the composed path matches an allowlist, and internal admin routes are not reachable from the public handler.

metadata.title: REST Invariant: Path Segments Are Encoded and Matched Against a Route Allowlist
metadata.lab_title: Exploiting server-side parameter pollution in a REST URL

rule_constraints.invariant: path_segments(client_input) == 1 and composed_path in allowed_internal_routes
rule_constraints.precondition: the front end builds a REST path from user input
rule_constraints.postcondition: encode input, reject traversal, and allowlist the composed route

text: Security invariant: the second-factor challenge is bound to the account authenticated in the first step, and no request field can change which account is being verified. Precondition: the login flow carries an account identifier into the second step. Postcondition: the identifier is derived from the session, a mismatch is rejected, and the attempt budget is keyed to the challenge rather than the session.

metadata.title: 2FA Invariant: Challenge Bound to the Session Principal, Not a Request Field
metadata.lab_title: 2FA broken logic

rule_constraints.invariant: challenge.account == session.first_factor_account
rule_constraints.precondition: the second login step accepts a verify parameter
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive the account from the session and key attempts to the challenge

text: Security invariant: the server issues a limited session after the first factor and upgrades it only after code verification, and every protected route requires the upgraded session. Precondition: 2FA is enabled on the account. Postcondition: pre-verification sessions can reach only the verification endpoints, and direct navigation or API calls return a denial.

metadata.title: 2FA Invariant: Server Enforces Verification on Every Protected Request
metadata.lab_title: 2FA simple bypass

rule_constraints.invariant: session.fully_authenticated implies session.otp_verified
rule_constraints.precondition: the login flow has a distinct second-factor step
rule_constraints.postcondition: issue a limited session and upgrade only after verification

text: Security invariant: each challenge permits a small bounded number of attempts, rotates or locks on exhaustion, and raises an alert on volume. Precondition: a valid password has produced a second-factor challenge. Postcondition: excess attempts invalidate the challenge and require a full new authentication, and the owner is notified.

metadata.title: 2FA Invariant: Per-Challenge Attempt Budget and Fast Expiry
metadata.lab_title: 2FA bypass using a brute-force attack

rule_constraints.invariant: challenge.attempts <= max_attempts and challenge locked on exhaustion
rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker holds a valid password
rule_constraints.postcondition: lock the challenge after the budget and alert on volume

text: Security invariant: a reset token resolves to exactly one account, that account cannot be changed by the client at confirmation, and the token is consumed on first use. Precondition: reset confirmation accepts a token and an account reference. Postcondition: the account is derived from the token, mismatches are rejected, and consumption is atomic.

metadata.title: Reset Invariant: Token Determines the Account Being Changed
metadata.lab_title: Password reset broken logic

rule_constraints.invariant: token.account == request.username and token.single_use
rule_constraints.precondition: confirmation accepts a token and a username
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive the account from the token and consume it once

text: Security invariant: every generated link uses a pinned canonical host from configuration, never a request header, and tokens are single-use and bound to the account. Precondition: the reset email contains an absolute URL. Postcondition: the host is immutable, spoofed headers are ignored, and a token redeemed from an unexpected client is rejected or flagged.

metadata.title: Link Invariant: Reset URLs Use a Pinned Canonical Host
metadata.lab_title: Password reset poisoning via middleware

rule_constraints.invariant: link.host == configured_canonical_host
rule_constraints.precondition: the reset email builds an absolute URL
rule_constraints.postcondition: pin the host and ignore client-supplied host headers

text: Security invariant: a password change applies only to the authenticated principal, requires the current password for that principal, and returns a uniform response for failures. Precondition: the form includes an account identifier. Postcondition: the identifier is derived from the session, failures are indistinguishable, and attempts are throttled per account.

metadata.title: Credential Invariant: Change Operations Are Bound to the Session and Throttled
metadata.lab_title: Password brute-force via password change

rule_constraints.invariant: request.username == session.principal and uniform_failure_response
rule_constraints.precondition: the change form includes a username field
rule_constraints.postcondition: derive the account from the session and throttle attempts

text: Security invariant: a login attempt carries exactly one credential pair, the parser rejects non-string credential types, and throttling counts each credential evaluated. Precondition: the login endpoint accepts structured payloads. Postcondition: multi-value credentials are rejected with a uniform error, and the per-account attempt budget is charged for every candidate.

metadata.title: Login Invariant: One Credential Pair per Attempt, Throttled per Account
metadata.lab_title: Broken brute-force protection, multiple credentials per request

rule_constraints.invariant: typeof password == string and attempts_counted_per_credential
rule_constraints.precondition: the login endpoint accepts JSON or structured bodies
rule_constraints.postcondition: reject multi-value credentials and count each candidate

text: Security invariant: failed attempt budgets are bound to the target account and cannot be reset by authenticating as a different account, and IP-level limits are additional rather than primary. Precondition: the attacker controls at least one valid account. Postcondition: per-account counters persist across source changes and resets, and interleaved logins do not clear them.

metadata.title: Throttle Invariant: Failure Budget Bound to the Target Account
metadata.lab_title: Broken brute-force protection, IP block

rule_constraints.invariant: account.failed_attempts <= limit and reset only by success on the same account
rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker holds a valid account
rule_constraints.postcondition: key the failure budget to the target account

text: Security invariant: every security or pricing decision compares operands of one canonical type produced by a shared parser. Precondition: the attacker can reach a workflow whose decision depends on a typed comparison, such as a plan check, role check, or quantity check. Postcondition: a value that cannot be converted to the expected type is rejected before any policy branch runs, and the rejection is audited. The check must run server-side in a shared policy layer that every channel, endpoint, and batch job traverses, and it must bind the decision to the authenticated principal and the persisted resource. Client-side flags, hidden fields, and UI gating are not controls. Missing, ambiguous, or conflicting values must fail closed, and every state change must emit an audit record that reconciles the business ledger with the entitlement.

metadata.title: Control invariant: CWE-1024: Comparison of Incompatible Types

rule_constraints.invariant: every security or pricing decision compares operands of one canonical type produced by a shared parser
rule_constraints.precondition: the attacker can reach a workflow whose decision depends on a typed comparison, such as a plan check, role check, or quantity check
rule_constraints.postcondition: a value that cannot be converted to the expected type is rejected before any policy branch runs, and the rejection is audited
